title: FedEx says coronavirus shopping helped offset commercial slowdown
summary: FedEx reported better-than-expected revenue and adjusted profit for its fiscal fourth quarter, despite a $334 million loss. The surge in residential deliveries due to increased online shopping during the coronavirus pandemic helped offset a significant slowdown in its commercial deliveries. The company incurred $125 million in COVID-19 related costs and will cut capital spending in the new fiscal year due to economic uncertainty.

title: Pollster with fake staff gave top grades to firms landing deals
summary: A firm named Black Book Market Research, led by Douglas Brown, whose rankings are used by major healthcare IT companies, is accused of using questionable methods. The company used fake staff on its website, lifts content from other research firms, and has a crowd-sourcing methodology experts compare to Yelp, which could lead to skewed results. Despite its claims of independence, Black Book is paid by the vendors it rates and has shown instances of working closely with companies like Allscripts to produce favorable rankings.

title: ‘Mad Men’ Rights Sold To Amazon/IMDb TV Globally, AMC & Starzplay In Complex Licensing Deal Made By Lionsgate
summary: Lionsgate has finalized intricate licensing deals for "Mad Men," bringing the iconic series to Amazon/IMDb TV globally, and back to its original network, AMC, and Starzplay. The agreement outlines various exclusive and non-exclusive international streaming windows, aiming to generate revenue comparable to its previous Netflix deal, which expired in June. The complete series on all platforms will include a blackface episode with a disclaimer explaining its historical context.

title: More Confirmation Online Retail Is Eating Traditional Retail's Lunch
summary: The Global X E-commerce ETF (EBIZ) saw significant growth in Q2, driven by companies like Amazon, Walmart, and Target, as online retail continues to take market share from traditional brick-and-mortar stores. Experts predict a sustained shift towards e-commerce, with U.S. online sales expected to reach $709.78 billion in 2020, representing 14.5% of total retail sales. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated this trend, making e-commerce a sticky theme for investors for years to come, despite a projected slight dip in share as consumers return to physical stores in 2021 before rising again in 2022.

title: Western Digital Launches SanDisk 1TB USB Type-C Pendrive for Smartphones
summary: Western Digital has launched a 1TB SanDisk Ultra Dual Drive Luxe USB Type-C Pendrive for smartphones in India, designed to help consumers easily transfer content between USB Type-C devices. The all-metal, high-performance drive offers read speeds up to 150MB/s and comes with the SanDisk Memory Zone app for content management. It is available from July 4, 2020, starting at INR 849 for the 32GB version and INR 13529 for the 1TB version, with pre-order discounts available.

title: Jeff Bezos's net worth reaches highest level ever after recovering losses from divorce
summary: Jeff Bezos's net worth has soared to a new record of $171.6 billion, surpassing his pre-divorce peak, driven by a 4.4% surge in Amazon's stock. This increase, amounting to $56.7 billion this year, highlights a widening wealth gap in the U.S. amidst economic downturns. Other tech billionaires like Elon Musk and Eric Yuan have also seen significant gains, while Mackenzie Bezos's net worth has risen to $56.9 billion, making her the world's second-wealthiest woman.

title: Purple Carrot Launches Frozen Meals at Whole Foods Stores
summary: Purple Carrot, known for its plant-based meal kit subscription service, is expanding into retail with a new line of frozen, single-serve meals. These 100% plant-based meals, developed with Conagra Brands, are now available at Whole Foods stores nationwide for $5.29 each. This move comes as grocery trends shift due to the pandemic, with increased online ordering, a resurgence in meal kits, and growing interest in healthy frozen food options.

title: HP reinvents the printer for the smart home
summary: HP has redesigned its Tango line of printers to integrate seamlessly into smart homes, moving away from traditional clunky designs. These new printers feature a minimalist design, fabric covers similar to smart speakers, and advanced smart functionalities, including control via the HP Smart app, voice commands with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, and automatic ink reordering through HP Instant Ink. The Tango aims to make printers more convenient and aesthetically pleasing for modern living spaces.

title: How Cloud Computing changes the way of business at Porsche
summary: Porsche is increasingly adopting cloud computing, viewing it as a critical enabler for innovation and digital transformation. The company hosted its first Cloud Innovation Day to educate employees, demonstrate its impact on the automotive industry, and explore its potential for enhancing customer experiences and internal operations. Porsche emphasizes that cloudification involves not just technology but also organizational and cultural adjustments.

title: Amazon delays Prime Day until October due to coronavirus
summary: Amazon has delayed its annual Prime Day shopping event until at least early October, due to ongoing disruptions caused by the coronavirus pandemic. The company advised third-party sellers to use the week of October 5th as a placeholder date. This delay follows previous postponements as Amazon works to normalize its logistics operations which were impacted by a surge in online orders and inventory shortages.

title: Trader Joe's coming to Page Field Commons shopping center in Fort Myers
summary: Trader Joe's is confirmed to be opening its first Lee County location in Fort Myers at Page Field Commons, occupying a 20,000-square-foot space in a former Toys 'R' Us building. This will be the second Trader Joe's in Southwest Florida and the 20th in the state, potentially boosting the successful shopping center and attracting customers from surrounding areas. Permitting documents also indicate a possible Ross Dress for Less in the same complex.

title: Back to the Future Celebrates 35th Anniversary with New Gigawatt Transformer
summary: Hasbro has launched a new Transformers-Back to the Future collaboration featuring GIGAWATT to celebrate the film's 35th anniversary. This limited-edition Autobot transforms from robot to time machine in 17 steps and includes movie-inspired details like Doc Brown-style goggles and a flux capacitor. It will be available on October 1, 2020.

title: Corsair Virtuoso SE Gaming Headset review
summary: The Corsair Virtuoso SE Gaming Headset offers a luxurious and comfortable design with solid audio quality, particularly for content creators, thanks to its excellent microphone. However, its audio can be treble-heavy and lacks strong bass, with full potential only unlocked via the iCue software on PC, limiting its performance on consoles. Despite its $210 price, its comfortable fit, long battery life (around 17 hours), and stylish RGB lighting make it a strong contender for PC-centric gamers and streamers, though those seeking superior bass or console-agnostic performance might prefer alternatives like the Astro A50.

title: Walmart Jumps With Amazon Prime Challenger Nearing Debut
summary: Walmart is set to launch "Walmart+", a subscription service priced at $98 a year, to compete with Amazon Prime. The service will offer perks like same-day delivery of groceries and general merchandise. This initiative aims to convert new customers gained during the pandemic into loyal subscribers, boost profitability in its U.S. e-commerce business, and gather valuable customer data.

title: Ideas innovadoras para restaurantes y bares por pandemia
summary: This article from Bancolombia offers innovative ideas for restaurants, bars, and discotheques to reinvent themselves during the pandemic. It suggests strategies for business continuity, catering to client needs like home cooking alternatives and virtual social events, and enhancing customer experiences with new service models. The proposals aim to help businesses adapt and thrive in challenging times while ensuring customer safety and satisfaction.

title: Google, Deutsche Bank Agree to 10-Year Cloud Partnership
summary: Google and Deutsche Bank have entered a 10-year cloud partnership, with Google providing cloud computing capabilities to Germany's largest lender. Deutsche Bank anticipates a cumulative return on investment of €1 billion ($1.1 billion) from this alliance, considering it both a revenue growth and cost-saving initiative. This deal represents a significant win for Google in the financial sector, as European banks increasingly adopt cloud solutions to modernize their IT infrastructure.

title: Here Are the Top 100 U.S. Retailers Ranked by Sales
summary: The National Retail Federation released its annual Top 100 Retailers report, ranking companies by sales from their most recent fiscal year. Walmart, Amazon, Kroger, Costco, and Walgreens lead the list, all operating with omnichannel strategies. Notably, only one pure-play jewelry retailer, Signet Jewelry, made the cut at number 98, though several others on the list also sell fine jewelry.

title: SCV News | Amazon Distribution Centers Coming to SCV
summary: Amazon has signed two leases for distribution centers in the Santa Clarita Valley, occupying an approximately 100,000-square-foot building at The Center at Needham Ranch and a 155,680-square-foot industrial lease at the IAC Commerce Center. This move is expected to bring 300 new employees, plus delivery drivers, starting operations in the third quarter of 2020, boosting the local e-commerce economy. Officials and real estate developers highlight the strategic location and the increasing consumer demand for shorter delivery times as key factors in Amazon's expansion.

title: First Amazon fulfillment center in Little Rock to create 1,000 new jobs
summary: Amazon announced it will open its first fulfillment center in Little Rock in 2021, creating over 1,000 new full-time jobs. The company is also planning a second, 85,000 square-foot delivery station to launch in late 2020, which will generate hundreds more full and part-time positions. The City of Little Rock approved the sale of 80 acres at the Port of Little Rock to Amazon.com, Inc. for the development.

title: CFO of Daytona’s CTO Realty Growth, former Consolidated-Tomoka, resigns
summary: Mark Patten, the longtime CFO of CTO Realty Growth Inc. (formerly Consolidated-Tomoka Land Co.), has resigned to take a similar position at an unnamed multi-billion dollar REIT based in the New York region. Patten played a key role in the company's evolution, including the launch of Alpine Income Property Trust Inc. and a joint venture with Magnetar Capital. CTO Realty Growth, known for its significant land sales around the I-95/LPGA Boulevard interchange in Daytona Beach, has begun searching for his successor.

title: Office Depot names former Amazon exec as chief technology officer
summary: Office Depot has appointed Terry Leeper, formerly of Amazon, as its new Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. This hire follows significant company changes, including job cuts and store closures planned through 2023, and comes as the company navigates expected declines due to Covid-19.

title: Santa Ana’s Nineteen01 Luxury Apartment Community Opens Southern California’s First Autonomous Convenience Store – QuickEats Close Convenience™ – to the General Public
summary: The Nineteen01 luxury apartment community in Santa Ana has opened QuickEats Close Convenience, Southern California’s first autonomous convenience store, to the general public. This store, powered by AiFi's computer vision technology, allows customers to shop and pay without traditional checkout lines. It offers residents and the community a fast and convenient shopping experience.

title: Nvidia market value closes in on Intel
summary: Nvidia is nearing Intel in market capitalization for the first time, fueled by a 70% stock surge this year due to the accelerated shift to cloud-based digital services. Nvidia's market cap has reached approximately $245 billion, just shy of Intel's $249 billion. This milestone would position Nvidia as the third-largest chipmaker globally by market cap, trailing only Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. and Samsung Electronics Co.

title: NVIDIA Now Most Valuable US Chipmaker, Intel Falls Behind
summary: NVIDIA has overtaken Intel to become the most valuable U.S. chipmaker, with its market capitalization reaching $251.3 billion compared to Intel's $248.2 billion. This surge is attributed to NVIDIA's strong financial performance, its dominance in gaming and data center markets, rapid adoption of its GPUs in AI, efficient cost management, and robust cash flow. The company's stock has shown exceptional growth, rallying 73.7% year-to-date and over twenty-fold in the last five years.

title: Why Digital Turbine (APPS) Stock is a Compelling Investment Case
summary: This article highlights Digital Turbine Inc. (APPS) as a compelling investment, based on Greenhaven Road Capital's bullish thesis. The firm, which pitched APPS in February 2020, noted the company's strong revenue growth in both U.S. and international markets through partnerships with major carriers and app companies. The article also points out increased bullish hedge fund positions and Digital Turbine's significant stock performance since Greenhaven Road Capital's initial recommendation.

title: Amazon rolls out bigger UPS-, FedEx-style delivery trucks
summary: Amazon is deploying a new fleet of larger, boxier delivery trucks, similar to those used by UPS and FedEx, to address widespread pandemic-related delivery delays. The company ordered over 2,200 heavy-duty Utilimaster "walk-in" trucks from Shyft Group to help fulfill its one- and two-day delivery promises for Prime customers, whose orders surged during stay-at-home orders. While these new vehicles can carry more packages, some drivers find them harder to maneuver than Amazon's previous vans.

title: Ocala Amazon warehouse sells to New York firm for $58 million
summary: The newly built Amazon fulfillment center in Ocala was sold for $58.4 million by CFI Ocala Property LLC to Lex Ocala LLC, a New York-based firm. The 617,000-square-foot warehouse is located in the Ocala/Marion County Commerce Park, a growing hub that has attracted other logistics centers and is expected to create hundreds of jobs. The article also touches on other significant property sales in the area, including a large horse farm subdivision and plans for affordable senior housing.

title: Rivian raises $2.5 billion as it pushes to bring its electric RT1 pickup, R1S SUV to market
summary: Rivian, an electric vehicle company, has successfully raised $2.5 billion in a funding round led by T. Rowe Price Associates Inc., with participation from new and existing investors including Amazon and BlackRock. This significant investment will support Rivian's efforts to bring its R1T electric pickup, R1S SUV, and electric delivery vans for Amazon to market in 2021, despite previous production delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and challenges in its collaboration with Ford.

title: Electric-Vehicle Startup Rivian Raises $2.5 Billion in Funding Round
summary: Electric-vehicle startup Rivian has successfully closed a new $2.5 billion funding round led by T. Rowe Price and participated in by investors like Amazon, Ford, and BlackRock. This latest investment brings Rivian's total funding since 2019 to approximately $5.35 billion. Despite the significant capital raise, CEO RJ Scaringe stated the company is focused on launching its R1T pickup and R1S SUV in 2021, and has no immediate plans for an IPO.

title: Rackspace Technology Files For IPO Four Years After Going Private
summary: Rackspace Technology, a managed cloud company, has filed for an initial public offering four years after going private. The company, which recently rebranded, aims to re-enter the public stock market, having transformed from a competitor to a partner of public cloud giants. Rackspace reported $2.44 billion in revenue in 2019 with a net loss of $102.3 million.

title: Expert tips for Macy's Black Friday in July Sale: Shop the best deals
summary: Macy's is holding a Black Friday in July sale with discounts comparable to its annual November event, driven by a need to clear inventory. A consumer analyst advises shoppers to capitalize on deals across homeware, kitchen items, clothing, and beauty products, especially Macy's exclusive items and spring apparel. The article highlights 25 top picks, from mattresses and small appliances to clothing, shoes, and beauty products, available at significant markdowns through July 13th.

title: An EV bubble? Startups ride Tesla hype to ‘staggering’ money
summary: Electric vehicle (EV) startups like Fisker, Karma, and Rivian are attracting significant investments, fueled by the soaring stock price of Tesla. Analysts express concern about a potential "hype cycle" given the large investments in relatively unproven companies. General Motors is also expanding its EV production, indicating a broader industry shift, while Tesla's valuation continues to defy traditional financial metrics.

title: Amazon Stock Price Could Gain 16% This Year Amid COVID-19, Cowen Says
summary: Cowen has raised its price target for Amazon to $3,700, making it the highest on Wall Street, and reiterating an "outperform" rating. This new target suggests a 16% upside for Amazon's stock, driven by continued robust e-commerce demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Analysts expect strong second-quarter results, with key drivers including AWS, advertising, subscriptions, and accelerating e-commerce growth.

title: Wells Fargo tells employees to delete TikTok from their company devices
summary: Wells Fargo has instructed its employees to remove the TikTok app from all company-owned devices due to security and privacy concerns, as well as the policy that corporate devices should only be used for business purposes. This move comes amidst broader scrutiny of TikTok's ties to China and follows a similar incident with Amazon, highlighting growing concerns among US policymakers regarding the app's data security practices. TikTok has stated it is open to dialogue with Wells Fargo to address any concerns.

title: Costco reports another surge in sales for June
summary: Costco experienced an 11% increase in June sales, mirroring a similar surge in March, driven by the Covid-19 pandemic. This comes as the company has seen "off the charts" sales due to the coronavirus outbreak and recently made a $1 billion acquisition to improve "last mile" delivery.

title: Amazon Makes Health Care Access Even Easier for Employees with Launch of New Third-Party Health Centers
summary: Amazon is launching Neighborhood Health Centers in collaboration with Crossover Health to provide convenient primary care services exclusively for its employees and their families. This initial pilot program will establish 20 health centers across five U.S. cities, aiming to improve healthcare access and preventative care for over 115,000 associates. The centers will offer a wide range of services, including primary care, prescription medications, behavioral health, and physical therapy, strengthening Amazon's comprehensive benefits package.

title: Independent Research Firm Cites Rackspace Technology as a Leader in Hosted Private Cloud Services in North America and Europe
summary: Rackspace Technology has been recognized as a leader in hosted private cloud services in both North America and Europe by an independent research firm, The Forrester Wave™. The reports highlight Rackspace's platform breadth, strong reputation for support, "Fanatical Support" philosophy, and innovation in managed services. Rackspace is considered a solid choice for both enterprise and SMB customers looking for hosted private cloud solutions.

title: New Amazon Shopping Cart Uses Cameras And Sensors To Let Shoppers Skip The Checkout Lane
summary: Amazon has unveiled a new smart shopping cart, called Amazon Dash Cart, that uses cameras, sensors, and a scale to automatically detect items shoppers place inside, tally the cost, and charge their Amazon account upon leaving. This technology aims to eliminate checkout lines and will debut at a new Los Angeles supermarket, with potential future expansion to Whole Foods or other retailers. The cart differentiates itself from competitors by not requiring scanning and can even detect when items are removed.

title: Google to launch 3 more tech certificates on Coursera
summary: Google is launching three new tech certificates on Coursera in data analytics, project management, and user experience design, costing $49 a month and taking three to six months to complete. These certificates aim to help workers affected by the coronavirus pandemic find jobs, with Google funding 100,000 need-based scholarships and considering completion equivalent to a four-year degree for relevant internal roles. This initiative expands on Google's existing IT support certificate program and includes plans for a hiring consortium, apprenticeships, and integration into high schools and community colleges.

title: Office Depot parent names former Amazon exec CTO
summary: The ODP Corporation, parent company of OfficeMax and Office Depot, has appointed Terry Leeper, a former Amazon executive, as its new executive vice president and chief technology officer. Leeper will focus on the company's technical strategy and modernization to support growth. This appointment is part of a trend among retailers to bolster their tech leadership as the industry shifts towards online operations, especially in light of the coronavirus pandemic.

title: NBCUniversal wades into streaming wars with Peacock
summary: NBCUniversal is launching its Peacock streaming service nationwide, offering a tiered service with free, ad-supported, and ad-free options. The company is betting on a hybrid model that includes news, sports, and a vast library of TV shows to differentiate itself from competitors like Netflix and Disney+. Peacock aims to attract consumers by replicating traditional TV economics while facing challenges like late entry into the streaming wars and distribution hurdles with major platforms.

title: Wayfair: The false conspiracy about a furniture firm and child trafficking
summary: This article debunks a bizarre conspiracy theory linking online furniture retailer Wayfair to child trafficking. The theory originated from QAnon communities, suggesting expensive Wayfair cabinets named after girls were hiding trafficked children due to their high prices. Wayfair clarified that product names are algorithm-generated, high prices reflect industrial-sized items, and price glitches explain other anomalies, firmly denying the baseless claims.

title: Equinix to build fourth Italian data center in Milan
summary: Equinix is constructing its fourth data center in Milan, Italy, named ML5, with an initial investment of about $51 million for its first phase. Set to launch early next year, ML5 will offer 15,000 sq ft of colocation space initially, expanding to 45,000 sq ft in total. The facility will be powered by 100 percent renewable energy and serve as a strategic interconnection point for Italian and international companies.

title: Charles Schwab says retail trading kept booming in second quarter amid market comeback
summary: Charles Schwab reported a significant surge in retail trading activity and new accounts in the second quarter of 2020, with 1.62 million daily active trades and 1.6 million new accounts added, including 1.1 million from the USAA acquisition. Despite this growth, the company missed analyst estimates for both revenue and earnings per share, primarily due to a decline in net interest revenue. Schwab also made "significant progress" on its pending acquisition of TD Ameritrade.

title: How Software-as-a-Service Can Optimize Patient Care Delivery
summary: The article discusses how Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) significantly optimizes patient care delivery by providing healthcare organizations with advanced digital tools and data analytics without the burden of in-house infrastructure. SaaS addresses critical issues like data security, clinician usability, and fiscal certainty by offering scalable solutions, continuous optimization, and fixed subscription costs. This approach allows hospitals to focus on patient care while benefiting from cutting-edge technology and insights from a vast array of patient data.

title: Veteran VC Kittu Kolluri has $216 million more to invest through his new firm, Neotribe
summary: Kittu Kolluri, co-founder of Neotribe, has closed a second fund totaling $216 million, significantly up from their $130 million debut. Neotribe focuses on investing in early-stage companies with breakthrough technologies and aims to fill a gap in the venture capital landscape, investing between $2.5 million and $5 million. Kolluri emphasizes their conviction-based approach, working closely with founders, and focusing on deep tech, data science, and engineering to solve complex problems in enterprise IT, robotics, diagnostics, and clean energy.

title: Star Critic of Big Tech Has Side Gig Working for Amazon, Apple
summary: Fiona Scott Morton, a prominent Yale economist and former Justice Department official known for her critical views on big tech monopolies, is also advising Amazon.com Inc. and Apple Inc. These two companies are currently facing federal antitrust investigations, creating a potential conflict of interest for the expert. Scott Morton's dual role raises questions about the impartiality of expert opinions in antitrust cases.

title: Halliburton to close its data centers, move to Microsoft Azure cloud
summary: Halliburton, one of the world's largest oil field service companies, is partnering with Accenture and Microsoft Azure for a five-year strategic agreement to migrate its data centers to the cloud by 2022. The move aims to enhance digital capabilities, drive business agility, and reduce capital expenditures, utilizing Microsoft Azure for storage, processing, real-time monitoring, and machine learning. This decision comes despite growing criticism of cloud companies' contracts with the oil and gas sector and Microsoft's own goal to be carbon negative by 2030.

title: Looking for an escape: Younger people more likely to say entertainment costs rose since COVID-19
summary: A global Ipsos survey reveals that a quarter of people in 26 countries believe entertainment costs (electronics, movies, books) have increased since COVID-19, with younger individuals (under 35) being most likely to report this. The article highlights the boom in streaming services and gaming during the pandemic, noting that companies quickly adapted to deliver content to homes. While some changes in consumer behavior, like higher Premium VOD use, are expected to persist, there are concerns about content production shutdowns and "streaming fatigue."

title: AWS and HSBC Reach Long-Term Strategic Cloud Agreement
summary: HSBC Holdings plc has selected Amazon Web Services (AWS) as a long-term strategic cloud provider to accelerate its digital transformation. This multi-year global agreement will see HSBC adopting AWS cloud services across its lines of business, starting with customer-facing applications and modernization efforts in its Global Wealth & Personal Banking segment. The collaboration aims to enable HSBC to innovate faster, enhance customer experiences through personalized banking services, and improve operational efficiency using AWS's compute, storage, analytics, and machine learning capabilities.

title: McDonald’s is Hiding Policies That Perpetuate Systemic Racism Behind Woke-Washing
summary: The ACLU criticizes McDonald's for "woke-washing," arguing the company's public support for Black Lives Matter is undermined by its internal policies that allegedly perpetuate systemic racism against its predominantly Black and Brown workforce. The article highlights issues such as the lack of paid sick leave, unaddressed racial discrimination and harassment complaints, and dangerous workplace conditions during the COVID-19 pandemic. It calls for McDonald's to implement real policy changes, like guaranteed paid leave, instead of relying on marketing campaigns.

title: Big Tech Has a Big Climate Problem. Now, It’s Being Forced to Clean Up.
summary: Apple has pledged to make its devices carbon-neutral by 2030, joining other tech giants like Microsoft and Amazon in ramping up climate targets. The company plans to reduce emissions by 75% in its manufacturing chain through recycling and encouraging renewable energy use by suppliers, offsetting the remaining 25% with reforestation projects. These voluntary commitments come as big tech faces increasing pressure to address its own contribution to climate change.

title: Jeff Bezos net worth 2020 as billionaire, American business magnate and Amazon.com CEO break stock record in one single day for Bloomberg World's Billionaires ranked list history
summary: Jeff Bezos gained $13 billion in a single day, marking the largest one-day jump for any individual in the history of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Amazon.com Inc. shares increased by 7.9% due to the rise in internet shopping, contributing to Bezos's net worth reaching $189.3 billion in 2020. His former wife, Mackenzie Bezos, also saw a significant increase in her wealth, and other tech figures like Mark Zuckerberg experienced growth during the lockdown period.

title: Amazon's corporate office diversity remains largely a mystery while other big tech discloses data
summary: Amazon's corporate diversity data, particularly concerning its management, remains largely undisclosed to the public, setting it apart from other major tech companies like Facebook and Apple. While there are indications of increasing diversity in its management, the specifics are not publicly shared. This lack of transparency contrasts with the practices of many of its peers in the tech industry.

title: Target’s fresh grocery pickup service expands to 1,000-plus stores in 47 states. Is it available at your Target?
summary: Target has expanded its fresh and frozen grocery Drive Up and in-store pickup service to over 1,000 stores across 47 states, nearing its goal of 1,500 locations by the holidays. The service allows customers to pick up hundreds of grocery items alongside other merchandise, with no minimum order or membership fees. This expansion comes as curbside pickup grows in popularity, especially amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Jeff Bezos is now personally worth more than the market valuation of Exxon, Nike, and McDonald’s
summary: Jeff Bezos's net worth surged by $13 billion in a single day, marking the largest daily jump recorded by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His fortune now stands at $189.3 billion for 2020, exceeding the market capitalization of major corporations like Exxon Mobil, Nike, and McDonald's. This increase is attributed to a 7.9% rise in Amazon shares amid optimism about online shopping trends during an economic downturn.

title: Amazon Pays a Fine for Crimea Business, but Occupied-Territories Policy Remains Murky
summary: Amazon was fined by the U.S. Treasury for sanctions violations by delivering products to Russian-occupied Crimea, yet the article highlights a significant inconsistency in U.S. policy regarding trade with various other Russian-occupied territories and disputed regions globally. The authors argue that the U.S. government's inconsistent approach to trade and labeling in occupied territories, along with varying corporate responses, creates an uneven playing field and undermines U.S. leverage against occupying states. They advocate for a comprehensive overhaul of trade policy to ensure consistency and effectiveness.

title: Meet Scout: Amazon is taking its Prime Delivery Robots to the South
summary: Amazon is expanding its Scout autonomous delivery robot service to Atlanta, Georgia, and Franklin, Tennessee, following a year-long test run in other areas. These cooler-sized robots help reduce human-to-human contact during the pandemic and meet increased customer demand, operating at a walking pace during daylight hours, Monday through Friday, and available only to Prime Members for Same-Day, One-Day, and Two-Day delivery.

title: Amazon introduces boxes that can be recycled into cat condos, forts and other creations
summary: Amazon is launching new "more environmentally friendly" boxes that can be repurposed into various items like rocket ships, cars, pet forts, robot costumes, or mini-golf windmills. These boxes are part of Amazon's "Less Packaging, More Smiles" program, aiming to reduce packaging waste with QR codes directing customers to creative reuse ideas. The initiative reflects Amazon's commitment to The Climate Pledge, having already reduced packaging weight by 33% since 2008.

title: Jeff Bezos' Net Worth Jumps $13 Billion USD in Single Day
summary: Jeff Bezos' net worth increased by $13 billion USD in a single day, setting a new record for the highest individual increase since 2012, driven by a 7.9% surge in Amazon's stock price. This boost pushed his total fortune to $189.3 billion USD in 2020. His ex-wife, Mackenzie Bezos, also saw her net worth rise by $4.6 billion USD, making her the 13th-richest person globally.

title: Food Bazaar Operator Acquires 2 Fairway Stores
summary: Bogopa Service Corporation, operator of Food Bazaar supermarkets, has acquired two Fairway Markets stores in Brooklyn and Queens. These locations will be converted to the Food Bazaar banner, though the terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. This follows previous bidding and acquisition activities for other Fairway stores after the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy earlier in the year.

title: Gold Is Within Striking Distance of Its All-Time High. Here’s How to Play the Rally
summary: The article discusses gold's rally, nearing its all-time high, driven by the ongoing pandemic, global stimulus packages, and the overvaluation of tech stocks. Author Frank Holmes suggests that the precious metal is in a secular bull market and recommends a 10% portfolio weighting in gold and precious metals. He also highlights the strong performance of precious metal miners and royalty/streaming companies.

title: Kroger Names Milen Mahadevan as President of 84.51°
summary: Kroger has appointed Milen Mahadevan as the new President of its subsidiary, 84.51°, a data powerhouse. Mahadevan previously served as Senior Vice President, Head of Client Solutions and Capabilities at 84.51° and played a key role in developing the company's strategies. In his new role, he will oversee day-to-day leadership and operations for 84.51°, aiming to deliver strong results for Kroger and its partners.

title: Flipkart buys parent Walmart's Indian wholesale business
summary: Flipkart has acquired its parent company Walmart Inc's Indian cash-and-carry business to strengthen its wholesale offerings and launch a new digital marketplace called Flipkart Wholesale. This deal aims to better compete with Amazon.com Inc and local players like JioMart in the crucial Indian e-commerce market, despite Walmart not being able to profit from the wholesale business since 2009. Walmart India employees will join the Flipkart Group as part of the acquisition.

title: Home Depot drops Ego power equipment brand, which lands deal with Lowe's
summary: Home Depot has decided to cease carrying the Ego brand of cordless outdoor power equipment as part of a "reset" of its inventory. Following this decision, Ego, developed by Chervon, has secured a new deal with Lowe's. This move indicates a significant shift in retail partnerships for the power equipment brand.

title: AT&T calls launch of streamer HBO Max a success despite business challenges posed by COVID-19
summary: AT&T declared the launch of HBO Max a success despite COVID-19 challenges, with 4.1 million subscribers in its first month and targets for 50 million by 2025. The service's broad content and existing library attracted customers despite initial delays in original series production caused by the pandemic. While revenue across AT&T's businesses fell due to COVID-19, HBO Max's performance was a positive note, though big theatrical releases like "Tenet" are still planned for cinemas.

title: Intel's 7nm is Broken, Company Announces Delay Until 2022, 2023
summary: Intel announced a significant delay in the rollout of its 7nm CPUs, pushing their debut to late 2022 or early 2023. This delay is attributed to a "defect mode" causing yield degradation, putting Intel approximately twelve months behind its internal targets for 7nm process. The company is now exploring contingency plans, including the use of third-party foundries for some components and entire chip designs, and plans to increase shipments of 10nm chips by 20%.

title: Streaming service Philo adds TV One to lineup, won't raise price
summary: Philo is adding TV One to its lineup of 60 pay TV networks, making it the first time the channel is available without a traditional cable or satellite subscription. This addition is part of Philo's commitment to diverse programming and will not result in a price increase for customers, maintaining its $20 a month subscription package. The move also benefits Urban One, as Philo becomes the first streaming cable TV alternative to offer both TV One and Cleo TV in its basic package.

title: Jefferson: Rackspace, you’re bigger, quieter and more indebted than we remembered
summary: Rackspace Technology, acquired by Apollo Global Management in 2016, is much larger and more indebted as it prepares for a new IPO. The company has completed four acquisitions, including one for $1 billion, and its debt has grown significantly. Originally founded in 1998 with strong local ties, Rackspace has become quieter and more corporate under Apollo's ownership, though it remains a significant local employer and charitable contributor.

title: These retailers filed for bankruptcy in 2020
summary: A report from S&P Global Market Intelligence shows that 40 retailers have filed for bankruptcy in 2020, surpassing totals for 2018 and 2019, with more expected. This surge, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, has led to numerous store closures and ongoing negotiations for struggling companies like J.Jill and CBL & Associates. Notable bankruptcies include Pier 1 Imports, Neiman Marcus, J.C. Penney, and Ascena Retail Group, highlighting the immense pressure on the retail sector.

title: Kroger building distribution center in DC metro area despite no physical stores nearby
summary: Kroger is reportedly making progress on a 350,000 square-foot distribution center in Frederick, Maryland, which will be powered by British automated warehouse technology company Ocado Solutions. This facility aims to provide online grocery delivery services to residents in the Baltimore, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C. metro areas, even though Kroger has no physical stores there. The initiative is part of Kroger's broader effort to expand its e-commerce capabilities, capitalizing on the increased demand for online grocery delivery fueled by the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Meeting The Moment: HPE CEO Antonio Neri’s Year Of Extraordinary Leadership
summary: This article highlights HPE CEO Antonio Neri's leadership during a tumultuous year marked by the COVID-19 pandemic and social unrest. It details his commitment to partners, the acceleration of HPE's edge-to-cloud Platform-as-a-Service strategy with GreenLake, and his focus on the company's culture. Partners commend Neri's authentic leadership, his financial support for the channel, and his vision for the future of hybrid cloud.

title: International Paper mill observing 25 years in Henderson, has been success from the start
summary: The International Paper mill in Henderson, Kentucky is celebrating 25 extremely successful years of operation. Starting as a MacMillan Bloedel Ltd. facility in 1995, it quickly achieved profitability and high quality production with a predominantly inexperienced workforce. Now under International Paper, the mill continues to be a stable employer, a low-cost producer of recycled containerboard, and a strong community partner, with a culture emphasizing teamwork and safety.

title: Bogopa Service Corporation acquires two Fairway Market stores
summary: Bogopa Service Corporation, operator of Food Bazaar Supermarkets, has acquired two Fairway Market locations in Red Hook, Brooklyn and Douglaston, Queens. These acquisitions will expand the Food Bazaar banner to 28 stores, with Bogopa paying $875,000 for inventory and $5,000 for equipment for the Red Hook store, and $100,000 base plus $800,000 for inventory for the Douglaston store. This move follows Fairway Markets' Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing, with several other locations still up for sale.

title: How to Survive the Future of Retail
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the dominance of "apex predator" retailers like Amazon, Alibaba, Walmart, and JD.com, transforming the retail landscape. Traditional businesses must adapt by focusing on distinct market positioning, re-evaluating physical stores as media experiences, and specializing in one of ten defined retail archetypes (e.g., Renegade, Activist, Storyteller) to survive and thrive amidst these giants. The article stresses that a clear, focused strategy is essential, as the pandemic has pushed society fully into the digital age, clearing the way for new retail concepts to emerge.

title: Pharmapacks Announces Growth Financing by GPI Capital and JPMorgan Chase Bank
summary: Pharmapacks, a leading e-commerce enablement platform, has secured up to $150 million in growth financing from GPI Capital and JPMorgan Chase Bank to accelerate its expansion plans. This funding will allow Pharmapacks to significantly expand its warehouse footprint, invest in brands and inventory, and deepen its offerings across major e-commerce platforms. The company, which achieved over $250 million in sales in 2019, anticipates achieving 70% year-over-year growth and potentially 100% year-over-year growth in Q4 with the opening of a new replenishment center.

title: Apple CEO Cook says his company is "uniquely American" with no "dominant market share"
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook will testify before the House Judiciary's Subcommittee on Antitrust, where he plans to argue that Apple is a "uniquely American company" that operates in a competitive marketplace without dominant market share. He will highlight the fierce competition in the smartphone market from companies like LG, Samsung, Huawei, and Google, and defend the App Store's model as beneficial for developers. Cook will assert that Apple has never increased its commissions and that its fees are comparable to or lower than those of competitors.

title: Walmart Business Model
summary: This article details Walmart's business model, highlighting its strategy of leading on price, differentiating on access, competing on assortment, and delivering a great customer experience. It covers Walmart's operations, history, ownership, mission statement, revenue streams (products and services), and competitive landscape. The article also provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of the company.

title: Apple tried to lure Amazon's video app by offering a lower 15% fee, email shows
summary: An email released by the House Antitrust Subcommittee revealed that Apple offered Amazon a reduced 15% revenue share for Amazon Prime Video subscriptions signed up through the app, a departure from Apple's standard 30% fee. This suggests that large companies may be able to negotiate more favorable business terms on the App Store, contradicting Apple's public statements about treating all developers equally. The revelation came during a Congressional hearing on Big Tech where Apple CEO Tim Cook testified.

title: Nvidia sets 16 new performance records in latest MLPerf AI benchmarks
summary: Nvidia's latest A100 GPU and its DGX SuperPOD system achieved 16 new performance records in the third annual MLPerf benchmark tests, showcasing significant advancements in AI training. The company's hardware excelled in new recommendation systems tests, Natural Language Processing, and reinforcement learning. This performance highlights a four-times improvement over Nvidia's previous DGX system, reinforcing its position in the AI hardware market alongside other strong contenders like Google.

title: CyberArk launches open-source Shadow Admin identification tool for Azure and AWS
summary: CyberArk has released an open-source tool called SkyArk to identify "Shadow Admin" accounts in Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services environments. These accounts, often overlooked due to their indirect privilege assignments, pose a significant security risk as they can grant full administrative power to attackers. SkyArk features AzureStealth and AWStealth modules that require only read-only permissions to scan cloud entities and their assigned permissions, providing valuable insights for both red teams (offense) and blue teams (defense) to enhance security.

title: Here’s what the CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook and Alphabet will say at Wednesday’s antitrust hearing
summary: The CEOs of Apple, Amazon, Facebook, and Alphabet are scheduled to testify before a House antitrust panel on Wednesday. Their prepared statements indicate they will argue that competition exists and their companies strengthen America. The executives, including Jeff Bezos, Tim Cook, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sundar Pichai, will appear via videoconference.

title: Clorox, Hershey, Amazon, Publix, General Mills Top ‘AXIOS-Harris Poll 100’ With Best Reputations of Most Visible Companies - Harris Poll
summary: The Axios Harris Poll 100 report identifies companies with the best and worst reputations among the most visible U.S. firms. Clorox, Hershey, Amazon, Publix, and General Mills ranked highest, demonstrating strong performance in areas like trust and crisis response, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Conversely, companies like Juul Labs, The Trump Organization, and Facebook landed at the bottom due to struggles with citizenship, ethics, and trust.

title: Apple Halved App Store Fee to Get Amazon Prime Video on Devices
summary: Apple Inc. agreed in 2016 to reduce its App Store fee for Amazon.com Inc. by half for subscriptions obtained through its Prime Video app. This deal was a result of direct negotiations between Apple's Eddy Cue and Amazon's Jeff Bezos, aiming to bring the Prime Video app to Apple devices and its TV set-top box. The agreement specified a 15% revenue share for new subscribers via the app, with no share for existing Amazon Prime Video users.

title: Apple smashes revenue estimates in record third quarter
summary: Apple significantly surpassed revenue expectations in its fiscal third quarter, reporting a record $59.7 billion, an 11% increase year-over-year. This surge was driven by increased demand for iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers as consumers adapted to working and learning from home during the pandemic. The company also announced a four-for-one stock split and confirmed a slight delay for the next iPhone launch.

title: Keith White – Puget Sound
summary: Keith White, SVP, GM, Hewlett Packard Enterprise GreenLake Cloud Services, was named a top Technology Disruptor by CRN in 2020 for his work in delivering an on-premises cloud experience that competes with major public cloud providers. White was handpicked by HPE's CEO to lead the company's GreenLake Cloud Services Business Group after spending over twenty years at Microsoft, where he significantly contributed to the growth of Microsoft Azure. He holds a bachelor's degree in business and economics from the University of Puget Sound.

title: Ryder Steps in as Amazon Restricts Third-Party Sellers
summary: Ryder System Inc. is positioning itself to fill the void left by Amazon.com Inc. after Amazon restricted warehouse space for third-party sellers. This move comes as Amazon aims to manage explosive growth in e-commerce and prioritize inventory, especially leading up to the holiday season. Ryder is offering alternative fulfillment solutions to these impacted sellers, emphasizing transparency and quick setup.

title: eBay CEO’s early wins have yet to erase Wall Street’s doubts
summary: eBay CEO Jamie Iannone's initial successes, including a sales surge during Covid-19 and the $9.2 billion classifieds business sale to Adevinta, have not fully convinced Wall Street investors who remain skeptical about the company's long-term growth and ability to compete with Amazon. Iannone plans to use technology to improve the shopping experience, focus on the $500 billion used items market, and streamline payments to attract new shoppers and sellers to ensure lasting momentum. Despite investor doubts and previous CEO's clashing with activists, some long-term investors like Smead Capital Management see value in eBay's steady growth and profitability.

title: Clorox tops corporate reputation ranking as demand soars over COVID-19
summary: Clorox has risen to the No. 1 spot on the annual Axios-Harris Poll 100 Corporate Reputation Rankings due to soaring demand for its disinfectant products amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Consumers rewarded companies that provided essential goods and services during the crisis, leading to a shift in rankings where health and safety became paramount. Other companies focused on essentials like Hershey, Publix, and Proctor & Gamble also saw strong showings, while those that faced safety concerns or failed to meet consumer needs, such as Boeing and Juul Labs, significantly dropped.

title: Apple Announces 4-1 Stock Split After Shares Surge Toward $400
summary: Apple Inc. announced a 4-for-1 stock split following a significant surge in its share price over the past year. The company stated this move aims to make the stock more accessible to a broader base of investors, with post-split trading beginning on August 31. This marks Apple's fifth stock split since going public in 1980, contrasting with other large tech companies that typically avoid such actions.

title: Indago 3 Drone From Lockheed Martin Selected By Swiss Army
summary: Lockheed Martin's Indago 3 drone has been chosen by the Swiss Army for tactical reconnaissance and surveillance. The contract includes the unmanned aircraft, spares, training, technological support, and additional systems. The Indago 3 quadcopter is valued for its ability to provide aerial reconnaissance in challenging environments and will be used for information collection, search and rescue, disaster relief, and battle damage assessment.

title: Alphabet Inc (GOOG) (GOOGL) Q2 2020 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: This is a transcript of Alphabet Inc.'s Q2 2020 earnings call. CEO Sundar Pichai and CFO Ruth Porat discuss the company's performance during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting a decline in advertising revenue but strong growth in non-ad sectors like Cloud, Google Play, and YouTube subscriptions. They also cover strategic investments in AI, commerce initiatives, and efforts to support users and businesses during the global economic uncertainty.

title: Tim Cook says Apple buys innovation, not competitors
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook explained the company's acquisition strategy, stating that Apple buys companies for their technology and intellectual property, which are then integrated as features into existing products like the iPhone. He contrasted this approach with other tech giants, implying that Apple focuses on innovation rather than eliminating competitors. Cook cited examples such as Touch ID, Workflow (now Shortcuts), Texture (now Apple News+), FaceShift (now Animoji), Siri, and P.A. Semi (for mobile chips) as acquisitions that enhanced Apple's product ecosystem, rather than acquiring competing businesses outright.

title: Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada Look Favorable Ahead of Earnings
summary: This article highlights the favorable positions of Ivanhoe Mines and Franco-Nevada ahead of their earnings reports, despite a general decline in S&P 500 profits and U.S. GDP due to the coronavirus pandemic. It discusses how certain sectors, particularly tech and metals/mining, have thrived, with specific attention given to Ivanhoe's copper production and Franco-Nevada's performance as a gold royalty company, both benefiting from rising metal prices and strategic market conditions. The author also touches on the broader market sentiment, gold's performance, and other economic indicators.

title: XPO says tech, automation interest is leading shippers to outsource more of their supply chains
summary: XPO anticipates increasing e-commerce volume and supply chain reshuffling will drive more shippers to outsource their supply chain management. Despite a 17% revenue fall year-over-year, last-mile segment revenue grew 3% due to high e-commerce demand during the pandemic. The company is also seeing customer interest in automating operations and nearshoring production, leading to new growth opportunities.
